tools.name: premiere_get_state
tools.title: Premiere Pro state
tools.description: Where Premiere Pro is right now: app version, the open project (path, name), every sequence (id, name, duration, frame size, fps), the active sequence with its playhead, in/out points and selected clips. Call it first, and again whenever the user may have changed something by hand. Read-only and cheap.

tools.name: premiere_list_items
tools.title: List project items
tools.description: The project's bins and items as a flat list in tree order: nodeId, name, kind (bin, media, sequence, clip), bin path, media path, in/out and duration, offline flag. Use it to find the nodeId of footage before placing it, or to check what is already imported. Filter by `kind`, `name_contains` or a starting `bin`. Read-only.

bin.description: Start from this bin: its nodeId or its path from the project root, e.g. "Footage/Day 1"; default: the whole project

kind.description: Only list this kind: media (items with a file), sequence, bin, or any

name_contains.description: Only items whose name contains this text (case-insensitive)

recursive.description: Include the contents of nested bins

limit.description: Most items to return; the receipt says when more exist

tools.name: premiere_get_sequence
tools.title: Read a sequence
tools.description: One sequence in detail (default: the active one): settings, playhead, in/out, every track (index, name, muted, locked, targeted) with its clips (nodeId, name, start/end/in/out in seconds, media path, project item, enabled, speed, selected, applied effects, Motion/Opacity or volume values and which properties are animated) and transitions, plus the sequence markers. Call it before editing so you address clips by nodeId. Read-only.

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

include_properties.description: Per clip: effects, Motion/Opacity values (video) or volume (audio), and animated properties

max_clips.description: Most clips to list across all tracks; the receipt says when more exist

tools.name: premiere_capture_frame
tools.title: Capture a frame
tools.description: Render one frame of a sequence to PNG and return it as an image: your eyes on the edit. Use it after every visual change at the moments that matter (first frame, entrance end, mid-hold, last frame) and critique it against TASTE: title-safe text, contrast, one focal point. Default time: the playhead; the time is snapped to a frame. Uses the QE DOM's exportFramePNG at the sequence's frame size; a sequence that is not active is opened first. Changes nothing in the project.

time.description: Sequence time to capture, in seconds; default: the playhead

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_import_files
tools.title: Import media
tools.description: Import files (video, audio, stills, .srt, .mogrt) into a bin, "Zenvi Imports" by default, created if missing. Files already in the project are not imported twice (`dedupe`): their existing items are returned instead. Returns the nodeId of every item for premiere_place_clip. Missing files are refused before anything is imported. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

paths.description: Absolute paths of files on this computer

bin.description: Bin to import into, created if missing; "Footage/Day 1" nests bins; "/" is the project root

dedupe.description: Return the existing item for files already in the project instead of importing them again

image_sequence.description: Import numbered stills as one image sequence (pass the first frame)

tools.name: premiere_create_sequence
tools.title: Create a sequence
tools.description: Create a sequence and make it active. `preset`: 1080p30 (default, 1920x1080 at 30 fps), 1080p25, 1080p24, 4k30 (3840x2160), vertical (1080x1920 at 30, social 9:16), square (1080x1080 at 30). Built from an installed sequence preset (never Premiere's New Sequence dialog) and set to the exact size and rate. Or pass `from_clips` to build it from project items with settings matching the first clip. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

preset.description: Frame size and rate (ignored with from_clips)

from_clips.description: Build the sequence from these project items, in this order, matching the first clip's settings

items.description: Project item nodeId: `node_id` from premiere_list_items or premiere_import_files

bin.description: Bin for the new sequence (path from the project root, created if missing); default: the project root

open.description: Make the new sequence the active one

tools.name: premiere_open_sequence
tools.title: Open a sequence
tools.description: Open a sequence in the Timeline and make it the active sequence (tools default to the active one). Changes only what Premiere shows, not the project; nothing to undo.

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name

tools.name: premiere_place_clip
tools.title: Place a clip
tools.description: Put a project item on a track at a time, optionally using only part of the source (`source_in`/`source_out`). `mode`: overwrite (default) replaces what is there; insert pushes later clips right. Default time: right after the last clip on the track, so repeated calls build a sequence in order. Video items bring their linked audio. The item's own in/out marks are restored afterwards. Cut on action; keep b-roll shots 1.5-3 s, talking heads 4-8 s (TASTE §6). Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

item.description: Project item nodeId: `node_id` from premiere_list_items or premiere_import_files

track.description: Target track, {kind, index} with 0-based index (V1 = 0); default V1

index.description: 0-based track index as in the Premiere DOM: V1 / A1 = 0

time.description: Sequence time of the clip's first frame; default: the end of the last clip on the track

source_in.description: Source in point, seconds from the start of the media; default: the item's in mark

source_out.description: Source out point, seconds from the start of the media; default: the item's out mark

mode.description: overwrite replaces what is under it; insert ripples later clips right

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_edit_clip
tools.title: Edit a clip
tools.description: One edit on a clip by `action`: move (`to` a start time or `by` seconds), trim (new timeline `start` and/or `end`; the source in/out moves with the edge), enable / disable, rename (`name`), speed (`speed` 0.5 = half speed, with `reverse`, `maintain_pitch`, `ripple`; QE DOM), delete (`ripple` closes the gap on the clip's tracks). move, trim, enable/disable and delete include the linked audio/video unless `include_linked` is false. Locked tracks, moves onto other clips and trims into a neighbour are refused, as are trims of retimed clips. delete is destructive. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

clip.description: Clip (track item) nodeId: `node_id` from premiere_get_sequence or a receipt

to.description: move: the new start time on the sequence

by.description: move: shift by this many seconds (negative = earlier)

start.description: trim: new start (head) on the sequence; the source in point follows

end.description: trim: new end (tail) on the sequence; the source out point follows

speed.description: speed: playback rate, 1 = normal, 0.5 = half speed (twice as long), 2 = double

ripple.description: delete: close the gap; speed: push or pull the clips after it

include_linked.description: move, trim, enable/disable, delete: also the clip's linked audio/video

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_razor
tools.title: Razor cut
tools.description: Cut clips at a time, like the Razor tool, so each side can be trimmed, moved or deleted. Default: every unlocked track with a clip at `time`; pass `tracks` to cut only some. Returns the nodeIds of the new right-hand pieces. Uses the QE DOM. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

time.description: Sequence time to cut at, in seconds (snapped to the frame grid)

tracks.description: Only these tracks, {kind, index} 0-based; default: every unlocked track with a clip at that time

index.description: 0-based track index as in the Premiere DOM: V1 / A1 = 0

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_set_clip_properties
tools.title: Set clip properties
tools.description: Static values on a clip's built-in effects: Motion (position in sequence pixels, scale %, rotation, anchor), Opacity (opacity %, blend mode) and audio volume in dB. Only the properties you pass change. An animated property is refused unless `clear_keyframes` (use premiere_animate to change keyframes). Respect the frame: keep faces in the upper third and text inside title-safe (TASTE §3). Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

clip.description: Clip (track item) nodeId: `node_id` from premiere_get_sequence or a receipt

position.description: Motion > Position [x, y] in sequence pixels from the top-left; [width/2, height/2] is the centre

scale.description: Motion > Scale in percent (100 = original size)

anchor.description: Motion > Anchor Point as fractions of the clip frame [x, y]; [0.5, 0.5] is the centre

volume_db.description: Audio clips: Volume > Level in dB (0 = as recorded, max +15; -96 = silent)

clear_keyframes.description: Remove the keyframes of an animated property you set instead of refusing

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_animate
tools.title: Animate a property
tools.description: Keyframes on a clip's Motion (position, scale, rotation, anchor), opacity, volume, or any parameter of an applied effect (`{effect, param}`). Times count from the clip's first frame; values use the units of premiere_set_clip_properties. TASTE easings map to Premiere interpolation: smooth/in-out/snap ease in and out (Bezier ease), out/entrance arrives softly, in/exit leaves softly, linear (opacity and volume fades only), hold. Defaults: smooth easing, replace existing keyframes. Typical: entrance 0.6 s, exit 0.4 s, scale 92->100 % on entry, Ken Burns 100->104 % over the shot; never linear on Motion. Clips with a speed change are refused. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

clip.description: Clip (track item) nodeId: `node_id` from premiere_get_sequence or a receipt

effect.description: Effect display name as in Effect Controls, e.g. "Gaussian Blur"

anyOf.description: A parameter of an effect applied to the clip

time.description: Seconds from the clip's first frame (0 = where it starts on the timeline)

value.description: position [x, y] px, scale %, rotation degrees, anchor fractions, opacity %, volume dB; effect parameters as Premiere shows them

easing.description: Easing of the segment from this keyframe to the next; default: `easing`

keyframes.description: At least two keyframes; sorted by time for you

easing.description: Easing for every segment (TASTE §2): smooth, out/entrance, in/exit, in-out, snap, linear, hold, or {x1, y1, x2, y2}

replace.description: Remove the property's existing keyframes first

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_apply_effect
tools.title: Apply an effect
tools.description: Add a video or audio effect to a clip by its name in the Effects panel (QE DOM), then set parameters on it through the component API. Unknown effect names are refused with close matches; unknown parameter names are reported with the parameters the effect has. For colour looks prefer premiere_apply_look; for keyframes use premiere_animate with `{effect, param}`. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

clip.description: Clip (track item) nodeId: `node_id` from premiere_get_sequence or a receipt

effect.description: Effect name as in the Effects panel, e.g. "Gaussian Blur", "Lumetri Color", "DeNoise"

params.description: Parameter values to set once the effect is on the clip

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_add_transition
tools.title: Add a transition
tools.description: Add a transition at a clip's edge (QE DOM): `at` end (default; the cut after the clip, or its tail), start (the cut before it, or its head) or both. Default Cross Dissolve for video (Constant Power for audio), 0.5 s centred on the cut (TASTE: 0.5 s within a scene, 1.0 s for a change of time or place; dips to black for chapter breaks only). Clips without media handles get a shorter or one-sided transition; the receipt reports what Premiere made. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

clip.description: Clip (track item) nodeId: `node_id` from premiere_get_sequence or a receipt

transition.description: Transition name as in the Effects panel; default: Cross Dissolve (video) or Constant Power (audio)

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_apply_look
tools.title: Apply a colour look
tools.description: Grade clips with a Lumetri Color look (added when missing, reused when present): clean (+5 contrast, +5 vibrance), warm-film (temperature +8, tint +2, faded film 8, saturation -6), teal-orange (teal shadow tint, orange highlight tint, saturation +6), moody (exposure -0.3, contrast +12, saturation -15, vignette -0.8), bw-contrast (saturation 0, contrast +25), scaled by `strength` (default 0.6: keep skin natural). Targets `clips`, else every clip on `track`, else the selected video clips. Lumetri parameters are found by their English names. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

items.description: Clip (track item) nodeId: `node_id` from premiere_get_sequence or a receipt

track.description: Grade every clip on this video track

index.description: 0-based track index as in the Premiere DOM: V1 / A1 = 0

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_add_text
tools.title: Add a title
tools.description: Add a title to the sequence on a free video track above the footage. Premiere's scripting API cannot type text into its own title templates. So without `image` or `mogrt`, Zenvi Link renders the title itself: a transparent PNG at the sequence size, drawn with the panel's canvas, placed inside title-safe, and saved next to the project in "Zenvi Titles". You can set `font`, `weight`, `color`, `stroke`, the soft `shadow` and a `box`. Lines break at your line breaks and at 32 characters, on word boundaries, never leaving one word alone. `image` places your own transparent PNG: one with the frame's aspect fills the frame, a smaller graphic sits at `placement`. `mogrt` uses an After Effects-authored Essential Graphics template, setting its text control to `text` plus its size and colour controls when it exposes them. Defaults (TASTE §1, §4): `style` title 72 px at 1080p (headline 96, subtitle 44, lower-third 54, caption 42), weight 700 (headline 800, subtitle and caption 500), colour #F7F7F5 with a soft shadow, on screen for 1.5 s + 0.3 s per word (at least 3 s for titles, 5 s for lower thirds). Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

text.description: The words; keep lines under 32 characters and break on phrases (TASTE §4)

font_size.description: Override the style's size, in pixels at the sequence's size

placement.description: Where an image smaller than the frame sits, inside title-safe (9:16: clear of the top 12 % and bottom 20 %); default: lower-third for that style, bottom-center for captions, else center

time.description: Sequence time of the title's first frame; default: the playhead

duration.description: Seconds on screen; default: reading time

track.description: Video track index (0 = V1); default: the lowest track above V1 that is free for the whole duration

mogrt.description: An After Effects-authored .mogrt with a text control

image.description: A transparent PNG title: the frame's aspect fills the frame, a smaller graphic keeps its pixel size

font.description: Rendered titles: font family; default Inter, then SF Pro Display, Helvetica Neue, Arial (TASTE §4)

weight.description: Rendered titles: font weight; default 800 headline, 700 title and lower-third, 500 subtitle and caption

stroke.description: Rendered titles: an outline around the letters

width.description: Outline width in pixels at the sequence size

shadow.description: Rendered titles: the soft drop shadow for contrast over video (TASTE §4: distance 0, softness 16 px at 1080p, 40 %); default true

box.description: Rendered titles: a bar behind the text, for busy footage

padding.description: Space around the text in pixels; default 0.4 x the font size

align.description: Rendered titles: line alignment; default left for lower-third and top-left, else center

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_add_marker
tools.title: Add a marker
tools.description: Add a sequence marker, or with `clip` a clip marker (Premiere keeps those on the clip's source item, so every use of that media shows it). Name, comment, duration (0 = a point), colour, type (comment, chapter, segmentation). Default time: the playhead. Use markers to leave notes for the editor and to mark beats and chapters. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

clip.description: Mark this clip instead of the sequence

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_add_captions
tools.title: Add captions from SRT
tools.description: Import an .srt file and turn it into a caption track on the sequence, starting at `time` (default 0). Format subtitle (default) or a broadcast standard. Style captions in Premiere's Essential Graphics panel; keep them inside title-safe and readable at phone size. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

srt.description: Absolute path to a .srt subtitle file

time.description: Sequence time where the file's 00:00:00,000 lands

format.description: Caption format of the new track

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_auto_reframe
tools.title: Auto Reframe
tools.description: Make a reframed copy of a sequence for another aspect ratio with Premiere's Auto Reframe (Premiere Pro 2020 / 14.0 or later): 9:16 (default, social vertical 1080x1920 from 1080p), 1:1, 4:5, 16:9. The copy keeps the source's short side and is opened. The original is untouched. Check the result with premiere_capture_frame: faces in the upper third, text inside the vertical safe area. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

motion.description: How quickly the framing follows the action

name.description: Name of the new sequence; default: "<sequence> 9x16"

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_scene_detect
tools.title: Scene edit detection
tools.description: Find the camera cuts inside long clips with Premiere's Scene Edit Detection and either razor them (`action` cuts, default, linked audio too) or mark them (markers land on the source items). Runs on every clip of a track (default V1) or on `clips`. Premiere is blocked while it analyses; long media takes minutes. The previous selection is restored. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

track.description: Video track to analyse, {kind, index} 0-based; default V1

index.description: 0-based track index as in the Premiere DOM: V1 / A1 = 0

clips.description: Only these clips of the track

items.description: Clip (track item) nodeId: `node_id` from premiere_get_sequence or a receipt

action.description: cuts = razor at each detected scene change; markers = add markers

include_linked_audio.description: cuts: also cut the linked audio

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_export
tools.title: Export a sequence
tools.description: Render a sequence to a file. `preset`: h264-high (default, H.264 matching the source at a high bitrate), h264-social-vertical (the same for a 9:16 sequence; others are refused, run premiere_auto_reframe first), prores-422, or the path of an .epr. Presets are found among the installed Premiere / Media Encoder presets. `range` entire, in-out or work-area. `via` media_encoder (default: queued in Adobe Media Encoder and started, returns the job id at once) or direct (Premiere renders now and blocks until done). Existing files are refused unless `overwrite`. Changes nothing in the project.

anyOf.description: Absolute path to an .epr export preset

output.description: Output file; its extension comes from the preset when missing; default: "Zenvi Exports/<sequence>.<ext>" next to the project

via.description: Queue in Media Encoder, or render inside Premiere now

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_export_xml
tools.title: Export FCP XML
tools.description: Write a sequence (default: the active one) as Final Cut Pro 7 XML (xmeml), Premiere's own exchange format, with warnings dialogs suppressed. Zenvi reads this file to bring a Premiere edit back (import_timeline_xml_tool). Default output: a new file in the system temp folder. Changes nothing in the project.

output.description: Where to write the .xml; default: a new file in the temp folder

sequence.description: Sequence id (`sequence_id` from premiere_get_state) or exact name; default: the active sequence

tools.name: premiere_import_xml
tools.title: Import FCP XML
tools.description: Import a Final Cut Pro 7 XML (e.g. a Zenvi export) into a bin ("Zenvi Imports" by default) and open the sequence it contains. Returns the new sequence ids. Media referenced by the XML must exist at its paths or Premiere marks it offline. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

bin.description: Bin to import into, created if missing; "/" is the project root

tools.name: premiere_save_project
tools.title: Save the project
tools.description: Save the project in place, or with `path` save it as a new .prproj and keep working in that copy (Premiere's Save As closes the original). Save after a batch of edits the user wants to keep. Changes nothing in the project's content; saving is not an undo step.

path.description: Save As this .prproj path; default: save in place

tools.name: premiere_run_script
tools.title: Run ExtendScript
tools.description: Escape hatch: run an ExtendScript (ECMAScript 3) snippet in Premiere and return its completion value as JSON. `app`, `qe` (QE DOM, enabled) and `ZenviLink` are in scope. Use only when no premiere_* tool covers the job; the snippet can change or delete anything. Premiere cannot group undo: each change is its own undo step (undoSteps counts them).

script.description: ExtendScript source; the value of its last statement is returned
